title: Table Matchmaking
body: Shown below are the chocolates and nutrition tables respectively. Match the following table method calls to the resulting descriptions of tables.\n##figure1.gif

figureAlts.figure1.gif: The image contains two tables and a matching exercise. The first table, titled "chocolates," has columns: Color, Shape, Amount, and Price ($). Row 1: Dark, Round, 4, 1.30; Row 2: Milk, Rectangular, 6, 1.20; Row 3: White, Rectangular, 12, 2.00; Row 4: Dark, Round, 7, 1.75; Row 5: Milk, Rectangular, 9, 1.40; Row 6: Milk, Round, 2, 1.00. The second table, titled "nutrition," has columns: Type and Calories. Row 1: Dark, 120; Row 2: Milk, 130; Row 3: White, 115; Row 4: Ruby, 120. Below the tables, there is a matching exercise with a list of function calls and a list of table descriptions. The function calls are labeled A to F: A is chocolates.group("Shape"), B is chocolates.group("Shape", max), C is chocolates.group(make_array("Shape", "Color"), max), D is chocolates.pivot("Color", "Shape", "Price ($)", max), E is chocolates.join("Color", nutrition, "Type"), F is chocolates.group(make_array("Shape", "Color")).
